title: Coefficient comparisons for inverse-purity Weil and counit reconstruction
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Use the small pro-etale categories $D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ of [def-pur-conventions], for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$: integral coefficients are completed and derived complete with uniform cohomological and Tor intervals, and field coefficients are scalar-localized/common-stage objects. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated finite type between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with smooth geometric base change $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$. Write $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$, for [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Use a strict datum $\varphi_K:G_YK\simeq K$ on $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ as in [def-pur-tate-datum]. Write $P_fK=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$, $F_f=Rf_!$, $E_f=Rf^!$, $a_{f,K}=\gamma_{f,K}:P_fK\simeq E_fK$ for the purity map of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] and its specified coefficient transports [sk-thm-purity-transport], $\epsilon_{f,K}:F_fE_fK\to K$ for the counit of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $t_{f,K}:F_fP_fK\to K$ for [def-pur-smooth-trace] and its coefficient transports. Use the source and exceptional data of [def-pur-tate-datum] and the compact-support datum $\varphi_{F_fM}=F_f(\varphi_M)e_{f,M}$ of [def-pur-compact-support-transport], where $e_f:G_YF_f\simeq F_fG_X$ is its specified semilinear exchange. All objects below are restricted to the constructible finite-Tor domains of these operations and comparisons.

Let $T_W$ be one of the following coefficient functors, with the operation comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and, for finite integral scalar extension, those of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]: derived reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ for $1\leq m\leq n$, integral-to-finite reduction, finite integral scalar extension, rationalization, finite coefficient-field extension, or passage to a common finite stage in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. At a ramified extension use its actual quotient-tower comparisons, without identifying equal uniformizer indices. A prime on a symbol denotes the corresponding object or operation after this coefficient change. Let $j_{W,N}:T_WG_WN\simeq G'_WT_WN$, $s_K:T_XP_fK\simeq P'_fT_YK$, $e_K:T_XE_fK\simeq E'_fT_YK$, and $r_M:T_YF_fM\simeq F'_fT_XM$ be the specified comparisons of the named operations, Tate data and semilinear compact-support exchange. For any datum on $N$ put $\varphi_N^T=T_W(\varphi_N)j_{W,N}^{-1}$.

These actual comparisons have the following identities, including their normalized tower realizations. The recovery formulas are
$$\varphi_{E_fK}=a_{f,K}\varphi_{P_fK}(G_Xa_{f,K})^{-1},\qquad \epsilon_{f,K}=t_{f,K}F_f(a_{f,K}^{-1}).$$
The Tate datum is the two-arrow source $\varphi_{P_fK}=(Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d)[2d]b_{f,K}$, where $b_{f,K}$ has target $(Lf^*G_YK\otimes^LG_X\Lambda_X(d))[2d]$ before $\tau_d$ is applied; $s_K$ is the source comparison of [lem-pur-weil-tate-datum-transport], and the second identity below is the coefficient clause of that lemma. One has
$$e_KT_X(a_{f,K})=a'_{f,T_YK}s_K,\quad s_K\varphi_{P_fK}^T=\varphi_{P'_fT_YK}G'_X(s_K),$$
$$T_Y(t_{f,K})=t'_{f,T_YK}F'_f(s_K)r_{P_fK},\quad T_X(a_{f,K}^{-1})e_K^{-1}=s_K^{-1}(a'_{f,T_YK})^{-1},$$
$$e_K\varphi_{E_fK}^T=\varphi_{E'_fT_YK}G'_X(e_K),\qquad T_Y(\epsilon_{f,K})=\epsilon'_{f,T_YK}F'_f(e_K)r_{E_fK}.$$
Moreover $r_M$ intertwines the coefficient image of $\varphi_{F_fM}$ with the compact-support datum induced from $\varphi_M^T$, for $M=P_fK,E_fK$. Here the exchange compared is the specified compactification mate/open composite $G_YRp_*j_!\simeq Rp'_*\bar g^{-1}j_!\simeq Rp'_*j'_!G_X$ of [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing], with $j,p,j',p',\bar g$ its compactification data over $S=Y$; no $k$-linearity of $g_{T,\gamma}$ is required. The equalities are between the specified strict-tower transformations before derived inverse limit at integral coefficients and their scalar-localized/common-stage images at field coefficients.

proof.text: Write $a=a_{f,K}$ and suppress $f,K$ when unambiguous; composition is read right to left. In [def-pur-tate-datum] the exceptional exchange is $a_{G_YK}B_K(G_Xa_K)^{-1}$, where $B_K$ includes the Tate arrow, so $\varphi_{P_fK}=P_f(\varphi_K)B_K$. Naturality of the purity isomorphism of [sk-thm-purity-transport] gives $E_f(\varphi_K)a_{G_YK}=a_KP_f(\varphi_K)$. Substituting into the defining exceptional datum gives $\varphi_{E_fK}=a\varphi_{P_fK}(G_Xa)^{-1}$. By [def-pur-smooth-trace], $t=\epsilon F_f(a)$; compose on the right with $F_f(a^{-1})$ to obtain $\epsilon=tF_f(a^{-1})$. The transported trace has this same definition by [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] and [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence].

proof.text: The coefficient compatibility of [sk-thm-purity-transport], with the specified comparisons, is $e_KT_X(a_K)=a'_{T_YK}s_K$. For finite quotients this is precisely [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]. Integral-to-finite reduction is the reduction assertion of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction]. For integral scalar extension, [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] identifies its exceptional comparison by the compact-support counit transpose and proves this equation for its simultaneous chosen family. The compact-support comparison used there is [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison], formed for ramification index $h$ at $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,hn}$, not by identifying uniformizer indices. Rationalization and finite coefficient-field extension use [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. Thus this equation uses the actual purity maps at every permitted stage.

proof.text:
The first source arrow in [def-pur-tate-datum] stops at $(Lf^*G_YK\otimes^LG_X\Lambda_X(d))[2d]$; the second applies $(Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d)[2d]$. For quotient and integral reduction use [lem-pur-weil-tate-datum-transport]. For finite coefficient extension use the specified source equation in [lem-pur-tate-source-field-comparison-descent], with its scalar functor $R=T$, $C=j$ and $a_P=s$:
$$s_KT_X(\varphi_{P_fK})=\varphi_{P'_fT_YK}G'_X(s_K)j_{X,P_fK}.$$
It concerns the complete source composite, including the commuting-pullback compositor for $fg_X=g_Yf$, not just the tensor comparison. Compose on the right with $j_{X,P_fK}^{-1}$ to obtain the required equation. Its integral source comparisons are those of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]; its localized/common-stage clauses give the field cases. The strict-source realizations are [lem-pur-tate-source-strict-system-identities]. In particular this step does not infer scalar/compositor coherence solely from tensor coherence.

proof.text:
For finite quotient changes the specified exceptional and compact-support comparisons identify counits by [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. Integral reduction uses [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. For integral extension put $T=C_{F/E}$, $r=c_{F/E}$ and $e=b_{F/E}$, using the canonical ordinary-tensor/strict-extension identification. By [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], $e_K$ is the adjoint transpose of $T_Y(\epsilon_K)r_{E_fK}^{-1}$. The defining inverse Hom bijection sends $e_K$ to $\epsilon'_{T_YK}F'_f(e_K)$; hence
$$\epsilon'_{T_YK}F'_f(e_K)=T_Y(\epsilon_K)r_{E_fK}^{-1}.$$
Compose with $r_{E_fK}$ on the right. Rationalization and finite field extension use the counit clause of [lem-coef-rational-operations], and common-stage arrows are their images. Every case gives $T_Y(\epsilon_K)=\epsilon'_{T_YK}F'_f(e_K)r_{E_fK}$. This compares the defined trace in Step 5; Step 7 then recovers the counit from trace and inverse purity.

proof.text: Now calculate the trace comparison from $t=\epsilon F_f(a)$ (Step 1). Naturality of $r$ gives $r_{E_fK}T_Y(F_f(a))=F'_f(T_Xa)r_{P_fK}$. Therefore Step 4 and Step 2 give $T_Y(t)=\epsilon'F'_f(e)r_E T_Y(F_f(a))=\epsilon'F'_f(eT_Xa)r_P=\epsilon'F'_f(a's)r_P=t'F'_f(s)r_P$, as required. Inverting $eT_Xa=a's$ gives $T_X(a^{-1})e^{-1}=s^{-1}(a')^{-1}$; multiply on the right by $e$ when needed below. Functors preserve inverses since applying a functor to the two inverse identities again gives the two inverse identities.

proof.text: Put $u=\varphi_{P_fK}$, $v=\varphi_{E_fK}$, $j_P=j_{X,P_fK}$ and $j_E=j_{X,E_fK}$. Naturality of $j$ at $a$ says $j_ET_X(G_Xa)=G'_X(T_Xa)j_P$. Step 1 then gives $v^T=T_X(a)u^T(G'_XT_Xa)^{-1}$. Using Steps 2 and 3, $ev^T=a'su^T(G'_XT_Xa)^{-1}=a'u'G'_X(s)(G'_XT_Xa)^{-1}$. From Step 2, $s(T_Xa)^{-1}=(a')^{-1}e$, so this last expression is $a'u'(G'_Xa')^{-1}G'_Xe=v'G'_Xe$, by Step 1 at the new coefficients. This proves the exceptional-datum comparison with the indicated direction of $j^{-1}$.

proof.text: Recover the counit using the trace comparison rather than changing its normalization. Steps 1 and 5, naturality of $r$ at $a^{-1}$, and $sT_X(a^{-1})=(a')^{-1}e$ give $T_Y(\epsilon)=T_Y(t)T_Y(F_f(a^{-1}))=t'F'_f(s)r_P T_Y(F_f(a^{-1}))=t'F'_f(sT_X(a^{-1}))r_E=t'F'_f((a')^{-1})F'_f(e)r_E=\epsilon'F'_f(e)r_E$. This is exactly the counit identity in the item.

proof.text:
Use [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing] over $S=Y$. It identifies the specified exchange $\xi_M:G_YF_fM\to F_fG_XM$ with the displayed proper mate followed by the open comparison, and identifies its quotient, integral-reduction and field coefficient images. For integral extension use [lem-pur-integral-scalar-isomorphism-exchange] with $g=g_{Y,\gamma}$, $g'=g_{X,\gamma}$, $c_f=r$ and $J=j$; its square holds for the specified $c_{F/E}$ and on $A_{E,n}\to A_{F,hn}$ systems. Thus in every case the coefficient square reads $F'_f(j_{X,M})r_{G_XM}T_Y(\xi_M)=\xi'_{T_XM}G'_Y(r_M)j_{Y,F_fM}$. For any datum $\varphi_M$, naturality of $r$ gives
$$r_M T_Y(F_f\varphi_M)T_Y(\xi_M)j_{Y,F_fM}^{-1}=F'_f(T_X\varphi_M)r_{G_XM}T_Y(\xi_M)j_{Y,F_fM}^{-1}=F'_f(\varphi_M^T)\xi'_{T_XM}G'_Y(r_M).$$
By [def-pur-compact-support-transport] these are the two compact-support data to compare. This works for both $M=P_fK,E_fK$; Steps 3 and 6 identify their transported input data through $s,e$. The hypothesis on this exchange is an isomorphism of underlying schemes, so geometric Galois pullback is allowed without $k$-linearity.

proof.text:
Work on uniformizer systems throughout. Let $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$ be [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. By [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps], its actual counit $\eta_N:\mathcal R\mathcal LN\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ is invertible for every normalized system, naturally in system maps. For any such map $u:N\to N'$ naturality gives
$$u=\eta_{N'}\mathcal R(\mathcal Lu)\eta_N^{-1}.$$
Consequently two specified normalized-system maps with equal total limits are equal after these canonical endpoint identifications; this uses the entire-system counit, not separate evaluations. The purity lift in [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], source systems in [lem-pur-tate-source-strict-system-identities], compact-support systems in [lem-coef-integral-compact-support], and exceptional/counit realization in [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] are normalized systems with these identifications. The strict exchange realization is [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing]. Apply $\mathcal R$ to the integral equations of Steps 1--8 and use the displayed conjugation to identify their actual realizations. Functoriality retains composition and inverse identities. This proves their equality in the derived category of whole uniformizer systems before applying $\mathcal L$; integral reduction is evaluation of these equations.

proof.text: For ramified integral extension the actual $F$-uniformizer system is restricted to indices $hn$, with composite quotient transitions, giving $B_n=\mathcal O_F/(\varpi_E^n)=A_{F,hn}$. The derived scalar systems and their proper/open comparison $\alpha^{\rm sys}$ are [lem-coef-ramified-scalar-system-transpose]. Their specified cofinal limit comparison is [lem-coef-ramified-scalar-exceptional-limit]; it identifies the limit of $\alpha^{\rm sys}$ with precisely $c_{F/E}$ on morphisms. The counit word is identified before projections by [lem-coef-ramified-scalar-counit-limit]. The transpose/limit identity of [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus] therefore identifies the limit of the system transpose with the same $b_{F/E}$ used in Step 4, by the inverse adjunction bijection. The pullback/tensor comparisons are the normalized actual-system realizations of [lem-pur-normalized-scalar-comparison-realization]; the exchange square on these retained systems is [lem-pur-integral-scalar-isomorphism-exchange]. Apply the full $F$-reduction functor to Steps 1--8 and restrict that equality of actual systems to $hn$. The counit conjugation of Step 9 identifies the specified normalized maps; the cited scalar and cofinal comparisons identify their limits and quotient projections. This proves the ramified system equations using actual uniformizer quotients, without reconstructing a full system from an unproved converse to subsequence restriction. Finally [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity, lem-pur-tate-source-field-comparison-descent] carry these arrows and equations through localization and a common finite field stage. All operations are on the stated constructible finite-Tor domains with uniform intervals.

The det-sp citations are gone. (3) Step 8 cites the new lem-pur-integral-scalar-isomorphism-exchange. Its square C_{Y'}G_gP_fM → P_{f',F}G_{g',F}C_XM is correctly typed and holds: G_g is transport along a site isomorphism, and the square reduces to ξ=ξ at F=E, is trivial at g=id, and is zero at M=0. Step 10 uses the ramified-scalar system-transpose, exceptional-limit and counit-limit nodes and normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus.
